title: Al-Hafiz, the Preserver
hook: the Preserver, who guards all things
tomorrow: food keeps appearing, and nobody brought it. where's it from?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Kabir, and a sentence that stops at greater. The line: greater. Today the week's Names come back, with one new one standing guard.

The airport curb, right after the hug. You watch them walk toward security until the crowd swallows them, and then you stand there a second longer, as if looking could keep them safe. Yesterday's question: who guards the people you love when you can't? In the Qur'an, a father faces that exact moment. Ya'qub has already lost one son. Now his other sons want to take the youngest on the road. And he says: Allah is better at guarding.
screen: `THE AIRPORT CURB.` → `A FATHER LETS HIS SON GO.` → `ALLAH IS BETTER AT GUARDING.`

segments.voice: That's Al-Hafiz, the Preserver, who guards all things. The Throne Verse says it of the heavens and the earth, in Pickthall's words: "He is never weary of preserving them." Never weary. No refreshing needed. Here's the line to tell a friend tonight. In a hadith the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, taught a boy, he said: be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. In Arabic, mindful and protect are the same verb, hafiza. Guard Him in your life, and you are guarded. Now the week, coming back. The Forbearing: three seconds slower than the room. The Magnificent: everything finds its size. The All-Forgiving: He covers. The Appreciative: nothing is too small. The Most High: the heavy thing goes on the floor. The Most Great: greater, with nothing after. And today, the one who keeps all of it, and all of them. Ya'qub still let his son go, and still told them to be careful. Guarding the people you love belongs first to the Preserver; your part is the du'a and the text that says, get home safe.
screen: `NEVER WEARY OF PRESERVING.` · `BE MINDFUL, AND BE PROTECTED.` · `SIX NAMES COME BACK.` · `YOUR PART: THE DU'A AND THE TEXT.` · then, large: `PRESERVED.`

segments.voice: Choose one person you love who's on the road, in a hard week, or far away. Send them one short line that asks nothing back: thinking of you, get home safe. Some say a du'a for them by name as it sends; either way, let the sit be the moment you hand them over.
screen: `ONE PERSON, FAR AWAY.` · `ONE LINE. GET HOME SAFE.`

segments.voice: Al-Hafiz. The Preserver, who guards all things and is never weary of it.
Keep this: preserved, the people you love included, even when your phone shows nothing. That's two weeks of Names, held.

howItsDone: Muslims ask Allah, al-Hafiz, to protect those they love, often with du'a for travelers; some recite the Throne Verse (2:255) before a journey and before sleep.
